feed.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?

entry.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
entry.summary:
Bitcoin addresses currently fall short as proper abstractions for spending conditions. The debate is often framed around which address type should be the default, but a deeper issue lies in how these addresses represent or fail to represent the underlying script requirements for spending funds. While having different, even incompatible, address encodings poses no significant challenge for technical implementors, it has become problematic for closed-source product providers who must balance technical possibilities with user needs and regulatory demands.
The open source community may see the value in adopting new output types like Taproot, yet widespread adoption is hindered by the decisions made on the proprietary side of the ecosystem. Businesses are highly sensitive to incentives and external pressures. Privacy enhancements, while technologically feasible, are not widely prioritized by average users and may even be perceived as regulatory risks by businesses. Moreover, transaction fee differences between Segwit v0 and v1 outputs are negligible given current low fee environments, reducing one possible incentive for change.
A universal bitcoin address format capable of communicating arbitrary scripts could streamline interoperability, but allowing unrestricted script data within addresses would introduce significant security and usability risks. This approach might create more problems than it solves, potentially increasing the likelihood of errors or exploits compared to the current system.
Wallet developers face limitations in influencing user behavior when support for advanced address types is inconsistent across the ecosystem. Telling users to request support from exchanges is ineffective, as users can easily switch applications rather than advocate for technical upgrades. Any efforts to encourage broader adoption of advanced output types need to consider the human element, user incentives, and ecosystem dynamics. Further discussion and collaborative action are necessary to address these challenges and promote wider acceptance of innovative Bitcoin features.
